author: The Infographics Show
description:
HP built its printer business around cheap hardware and expensive ink. Then it went even further.

With Dynamic Security, some HP printers can reject third-party or refilled cartridges. Its Instant Ink subscription can also disable cartridges when a customer stops paying, even if ink is still inside. The strategy was designed to keep users locked into HP’s ecosystem. But the backlash is growing.
HP has faced lawsuits, regulatory action, and increasing frustration from customers who feel they no longer fully control the hardware they paid for. At the same time, competitors are pushing refillable ink-tank printers that can run for years without constant cartridge replacements. And now HP is selling ink-tank printers too.

The company that helped create the cartridge subscription problem may be getting forced to compete against it.



Narrated by: Josh Risser
